name: Switzerland
summary_text: Switzerland is a very safe destination for transgender visitors. Legal gender recognition has worked by self-declaration since January 2022 — a personal declaration before the civil registrar, with no court or medical requirements (binary male/female only; no non-binary marker). Same-sex marriage has been legal since 2022 (approved by referendum), gender-neutral rape law took effect in 2024, and employers have a legal duty of care toward trans employees. General crime is exceptionally low. The notable legislative shortcoming — flagged by the ILGA Rainbow Map and by the government's own review — is that the criminal hate-crime and hate-speech provision (Article 261bis) covers sexual orientation but not gender identity. So a person targeted specifically for being trans does not benefit from that aggravation in criminal law, though the protections available through employment and constitutional law are broader. Reported hate crimes against LGBTIQ people have risen about fivefold since 2020 (around six per week, but from a low absolute base of ~309 cases in 2024). The federal government adopted Switzerland's first National Action Plan against LGBTIQ hate crime in January 2026 (running to 2030), signalling a pro-trans institutional direction. There is no rollback movement.

sources.title: Rights of LGBTIQ persons
sources.claim_summary: Swiss Federal Office for Gender Equality official page: since 1 July 2020, public incitement to hatred/discrimination based on sexual orientation is punishable (Art. 261bis Criminal Code); 'Marriage for All' in force since 1 July 2022; covers LGBTIQ rights developments.

sources.title: Gender identity in the Swiss civil status register ‒ Community & Support ‐ EPFL
sources.claim_summary: EPFL page on gender identity in the Swiss civil status register: since 1 January 2022, any person registered in a Swiss municipality may change their sex marker and/or first name by personal declaration before a civil registrar - no court or medical requirement; changes are generally limited to binary categories, with some cantonal variation.

sources.title: Hundreds of Swiss change gender using simplified process - SWI swissinfo.ch
sources.claim_summary: Swissinfo: hundreds of people in Switzerland have changed their legal gender using the simplified self-declaration process introduced in 2022.

sources.title: Six anti-LGBTQ+ hate crimes reported a week in Switzerland - SWI swissinfo.ch
sources.claim_summary: Swissinfo: Switzerland records roughly six hate crimes per week against LGBTIQ people (based on monitoring reports).

sources.title: National Action Plan to combat hate crime against LGBTIQ Persons
sources.claim_summary: Swiss Federal Office for Gender Equality: on 28 January 2026 the Federal Council adopted the first National Action Plan to combat hate crimes against LGBTIQ persons 2026-2030, with three pillars - victim support and protection, prevention, and monitoring of violence.

sources.title: Swiss government unveils new measures to protect LGBTQI+ people from hate crimes - SWI swissinfo.ch
sources.claim_summary: Swissinfo coverage of the same first national action plan against anti-LGBTIQ hate crimes (2026).

sources.title: LGBT Rights in Switzerland: Protections and Limits - LegalClarity
sources.claim_summary: LegalClarity overview (June 2026): marriage equality since July 2022 (64.1% referendum approval); criminal-law protection against sexual-orientation discrimination since 2020; streamlined legal gender change since January 2022. Notes gaps: gender identity is not fully covered by the criminal anti-discrimination provision, and conversion therapy and surrogacy remain unregulated.

sources.title: The legal framework | trans welcome
sources.claim_summary: trans welcome platform (Swiss): the legal framework for trans people at work - employers' duty of care under Art. 328 OR and the Equality Act (GLG); employees may use their preferred name and gender at work without official change; employers must keep trans identity confidential; solutions for showers/toilets/cloakrooms must respect everyone's personal rights; the trans person may wear service clothing matching their gender identity.

sources.title: Switzerland - Rainbow Map
sources.claim_summary: ILGA-Europe Rainbow Map country page for Switzerland: overall index score and per-category compliance breakdown (after the 2021 self-determination and discrimination votes).

OSCE/ODIHR 2024 Hate Crime Report for Switzerland: Switzerland regularly reports hate-crime data; the Criminal Code has no general hate-crime provision - hate crimes are addressed under anti-discrimination provisions (Art. 261bis); ODIHR notes recording does not sufficiently distinguish hate crimes and police do not record bias motivation.

sources.title: Non-discrimination - UNHCR Switzerland
sources.claim_summary: UNHCR Switzerland page: everyone in Switzerland has the right to equal treatment; discrimination based on sexual orientation and gender identity is prohibited; LGBTIQ+ people enjoy equal rights; same-sex couples can marry since 1 July 2022; lists reporting mechanisms and support organisations.
